about: The gold tier 3 CT dataset's members: CT studies whose field holds the whole spine, C2 to the sacrum, with a person's annotation (the owner's tiers of 2026-10-27; a machine mask never raises a tier), admitted by the field test of rule version 3 (whole_rule; data/gold3-ct/admission.json). tools/gold3_ct.py reads this file, builds the dataset's index from it and the files it names, and holds it to its shape. Confidential, like the rest of SchwingNet: nothing here goes to a public place.
asked: the owner, 2026-10-27 22:49 UTC: "i want all the gold tier 3 CT data as its own dataset, with a indexable database, an artefact, and anything i need to use it in the workflow, including anomaly statistics, and quality assurance they are true anomalies"
tiers: gold = C2 to the sacrum in one study; silver = partial. 1 = a real CT and X-ray pair with a person's annotation, 2 = the pair without, 3 = one modality with a person's annotation, 4 = one modality without. Machine masks never raise a tier.

whole_rule.rule: Rule 2 with the owner's two ends of 2026-10-29: a CT is admitted when its field holds the foot of C2 and the top of the sacrum, whatever its masks hold. A level is drawn at 200 voxels or more. C2 drawn is in view unless the field's top cuts the level below it too; one not drawn is in view when the field's top lies above where C2's foot lies in 95 of 100 spines, counted from the head-most drawn level. The sacrum drawn is in view however little of it the field holds, a level above it that runs on to the field's foot flagged (level_past_sacrum_top); one not drawn is in view when the field's foot lies below where the sacrum's top lies in 95 of 100 spines, from the foot-most drawn level. The tables are measured on the members' own whole spines (the 5th and 95th percentiles). The field is measured over the column, and at the image's own edge over the column where a TotalSegmentator grid is padded. A study at neither end clearly in or out is a border case, silver 3 until a person's look. A level the release does not draw is completed by a segmenter, kept as a machine mask of its own and never raising a tier; one name the column skips between levels whose centres stand no farther apart than the study's own spacing of neighbours allows is a count variant, never a level to add. ENHANCE.PET's verdicts match version 1's tiers study for study but 1379, whose masks draw no C2 and whose field holds C2's foot: gold 3 while a segmenter adds C2.
whole_rule.asked: the owner, 2026-10-28 22:58 UTC (#443's question): "if the full spune is in view in the volume, and just missing a mask or two, that should just be completed using a segmentation software of choice ... i dont think i should leave out any spines that have ct volumes with the full spine in view"; and for version 3, 2026-10-29 12:58 UTC: "If the top of the sacrum is visible that is acceptable, which I believe is all of them but check" and "Same for the bottom c2"
whole_rule.source: tools/gold3_field.py (the rule, its thresholds and checks); docs/research/gold3-ct/ADMISSION.md (every count); docs/research/gold3-ct/README.md section 2 (why)

previous.rule: A CT is admitted when its field holds C2 and the top of the sacrum, whatever its masks hold. A level is drawn at 200 voxels or more. C2 drawn is in view unless the field's top cuts the level below it too; the sacrum drawn is in view when the field holds 20 mm of it below its top; a sacrum the field's foot cuts short of that makes the end out when the foot-most level above it is cut too, and a border case otherwise, as is a sacrum in view beside a level above it that runs on to the field's foot. One not drawn is placed from the nearest drawn level by tables measured on the members' own whole spines (the 5th and 95th percentiles), with 20 mm of S1 asked below the sacrum's top. The field is measured over the column, and at the image's own edge over the column where a TotalSegmentator grid is padded. A study at neither end clearly in or out is a border case, silver 3 until a person's look. A level the release does not draw is completed by a segmenter, kept as a machine mask of its own and never raising a tier; one name the column skips between levels whose centres stand no farther apart than the study's own spacing of neighbours allows is a count variant, never a level to add. ENHANCE.PET's verdicts, each study judged once on its repaired mask where it has one, match version 1's tiers study for study.

previous.rule: C2 and the sacrum each hold at least 200 voxels; every level from C2 to T12 is labelled; no space wider than 20 mm lies between consecutive labels above T12. A lumbar label missing or extra never drops a spine (the owner, 2026-10-27 17:10 UTC); an absent L5 is the common case and is reported as a variant, and any other lumbar gap is whole and listed for a look.
previous.source: bordercall holdings/count_enhance_pet.py (MIN_VOXELS, UNLABELLED_GAP_MM, LUMBAR_SPACE_FROM, class_of), the rule of the TotalSegmentator count before it

person_key.rule: <member>:<native id>, one spelling: enhance_pet:0001, verse:verse547 (data/splits/anomaly-holdout.json's spelling), totalsegmentator:<sid>. The split part is data/splits/rule.json's hash of that literal string, as tools/catalog.py computes it, so the spelling decides the part.
person_key.leakage: ENHANCE.PET carries no person id: autoPET's 1,014 studies are 900 persons (Gatidis S et al., Scientific Data 2022;9:601), and Leipzig and Careggi give none at all, so each study is its own person key and a person with two studies may sit in two parts. The risk is at most 114 autoPET repeats; it is recorded, not removed.

scheme.ribs: left rib k = k (1-13), right rib k = 13 + k (14-26), sternum 27; rib k's own vertebra is label k + 7, so rib 13's own body is the one this scheme names L1 (20)
scheme.canonical: 1-19 stay; L1-L6 (20-25) are canonical 21-26; the sacrum (28) is canonical 27; the hips (26, 27) are background. Never VERSE_TO_CANONICAL, which would make the right hip the sacrum and the sacrum a T13.

held.definition: A study is held when its CT and its masks are on the grid under the member's canonical root on the data root (grid.root) and every one of those files hashes to the sha256 this repository records for it. A copy anywhere else (a grid home, the Claude project's files, a public bucket, a thread's container) is a copy, readable but not held; a file whose bytes differ from the record is not held. A member's grid.held is checked (with the date and the job), unchecked or not_held; never true until a grid check has compared the sums.
held.why: Rows name files by sha256, so a study used for truth or training must be the file its facts were read from; a copy outside the data root may move or be cleaned away. data/sources/<source>.json's reach held (on the grid now) says the same at a source's level; this is it at a study's.

auto_anatomist.why: data/recipes/non-commercial.json allows open, share-alike and non-commercial with no owner review, so it takes all three whole (TotalSegmentator open, VerSe share-alike, ENHANCE.PET non-commercial as one); recommended on the owner's behalf for him to overrule. A commercial network would take TotalSegmentator alone, with ENHANCE.PET's Leipzig and Careggi only after a per-site split and every class first confirmed by the owner, and VerSe only under commercial-share-alike after counsel; loosening a class is the owner's alone.
